headline: Approved variance and relief requests for 279 Western Avenue and 69 Dollivers Neck Drive, and a subdivision water quality study for 187 Atlantic St.
summary: Approved septic variance and relief requests for 279 Western Avenue. Granted septic variance requests for 69 Dollivers Neck Drive, and approved a subdivision water quality study for seven lots at 187 Atlantic St. Also discussed enforcement for tobacco products without FDA approval, EWS Suitability Subcommittee guidance, and other updates.
decisions: Approved the June 4, 2026 meeting minutes as written, 4-0.
Approved the variance and relief requests for 279 Western Avenue, 4-0.
Granted the septic variance requests for 69 Dollivers Neck Drive, 4-0.
Approved the subdivision water quality study for 187 Atlantic St, 4-0.
Agreed to have the approval letter for 187 Atlantic St sent, with a comment about using actual site numbers if modeling numbers vary.
Agreed that the site suitability decision is explicitly included in all third party reviews, with its rationale stated in the decision.
Agreed that products bought from a distributor must be on the approved list, or have documentation showing otherwise.
Agreed that no further inspections are required for the Brian Pollard rental properties after five random inspections.

plain_text:
CITY OF GLOUCESTER 
Board of Health Meeting 
July 9, 2026, 5:30 p.m. 
Harbormaster Conference Room 
Minutes 
 
Board members present: Chairperson: Joseph Rosa; Vice-Chairperson: Dr. Eric Kaplan; Jesse 
Dole; and Thomas Markert. Absent: Erin George.  
 
Also present: Health Director: Dominique Hurley; Sanitarian: Cody Smith; Regional Prevention 
Director: Chelsea Goldstein-Walsh; Assistant Health Director: Gabrielle White; Administrative 
Assistant: Alison Battle; and Advisor to the Septic Review Subcommittee: Dave Sargent. 
 
The meeting started at 5:30 p.m.  
 
Public Oral Communication: 
  
There was no “Public Oral Communication”.  
 
Approval of Minutes: 
                  
MOTION by Dr. Kaplan to approve the Gloucester Board of Health minutes of the meeting of 
June 4th, 2026 as written. Seconded by Mr. Dole. Carried 4-0.  
 
279 Western Avenue - Designer Dan Johnson - Septic Variance and Relief Requests: 
 
Gloucester Onsite Waste Water Regulations Variance Request  
● Request reduction of the relocated garage to not be within 5 feet of where 10 feet is 
required of the new leaching area or any other septic system component (Reference 
GOWR 211 Table 1).  
 
Local Upgrade Approval Relief Request  
● Request reduction from the leaching area to the property line from 10 feet to 6 feet, 310 
CMR 15.211 and 15.405(1) (a).  
 
Dan Johnson, engineer for Domestic Septic Design appeared before the Board on behalf of the 
homeowner. He stated that the proposed design is to upgrade a failing system.  He gave a brief 
overview of the proposed request for relief.  
 
Mr. Smith reviewed the proposed variance request and the four local upgrades with Board 
members. He stated that the proposed requests are for an upgrade, so it is not for an increase of 
flow. He stated that there are two septic systems on the lot and both have failed. He stated that 
the Health Department suggests approving the variance and the relief requests. He stated that
Page 2 
Minutes of the Board of Health 
July 9, 2026 
 
he spoke with the engineer and he told him that if the applicant really wants to try to have that 
reduction in groundwater in conjunction with all this, then they need to make sure they're not 
paving the site, because we really want to make sure they're getting oxygen in there.  
 
Mr. Sargent stated that he would request that the leaching chambers that are next to that catch 
basin are abandoned. Mr. Smith responded that the engineer does have the one note, which 
says that everything needs to be abandoned per the code, and he can include an extra note 
because of the sensitive nature of the area in the plan approval. 
 
Chairperson Rosa asked if anyone in the audience would like to speak for or against the request 
for relief. There was no one.  
 
MOTION by Mr. Rosa that the Board of Health approve the variance request and the relief 
request as written on the agenda for 279 Western Avenue. Seconded by Dr. Kaplan. Carried 
4-0.  
 
69 Dollivers Neck Drive - Septic Variance and Relief Request: 
 
Gloucester Onsite Waste Water Regulations Variance Request  
● Situate a septic system 164 feet away from Mean High Water while using advanced 
treatment, where the Gloucester Onsite Wastewater Regulations (Table 1) require the 
setback to be 200 feet.  
● Situate a septic system 141 feet away from the salt marsh, where the Gloucester Onsite 
Wastewater Regulations (Table 1) require the setback to be 200 feet.  
● Situate a septic system and tanks 64 feet away from the FEMA VE zone where the 
Gloucester Onsite Wastewater Regulations (Table 1) require the setback to be 200 feet.  
 
John Judd, engineer for Gateway Engineers, appeared before the Board on behalf of the 
homeowner. He gave an overview of the proposed plan and the variance requests.  
 
Mr. Smith gave an overview of the variance request. He stated that his recommendation is to 
approve the 3 variances and 2 local upgrade approvals based on manifestly unjust, also to deny 
this person would lose use of their home.   
 
Mr. Sargent stated that the proposed plan is an improvement to what exists currently.   
 
MOTION by Dr. Kaplan that the Board of Health grant the variance requests for 69 Dollivers 
Neck Drive as outlined on the agenda. Seconded by Mr. Dole. Carried 4-0.  
 
Review for Approval: 187 Atlantic St Subdivision Water Quality Assessment: 
 
Mr. Smith gave an overview of the seven-lot subdivision plan that had to go through the 
Subdivision Water Quality Assessment.
Page 3 
Minutes of the Board of Health 
July 9, 2026 
 
Mr. Dole asked if there was buildable space behind the seven lots. Mr. Smith responded that 
right now the seven lots were done under an ANR, not done under a subdivision; so when the 
applicant first came forward, a couple years ago, they submitted something where they were 
planning on possibly developing this back area. He stated that he thinks they're trying to work 
on getting these ANR lots developed. He stated that he did take the liberty of drafting a letter, 
for the Board's approval if they decide to go that route and the approval letter that is drafted 
does specify that this subdivision water quality study is only valid for these seven lots.  
 
Mr. Smith stated that his recommendation would be to approve the subdivision water quality 
assessment, based on the standards that they've met. He stated that the third party's 
recommendation is similar and he did share that letter with the Board, although late.  
 
Chairperson Rosa asked if the overall approval of the development will necessitate yearly 
monitoring for three years. Mr. Smith responded that the approval of this report then puts it into 
a sampling schedule, so they will have to do another, almost what would be considered like a 
baseline sample again after all the roads are in and after all the drainage structures are in and 
then after the system has been in use for a year they will have to sample again.   
 
 A representative from the Procopio Company appeared before the Board. He stated that there 
are also representatives present from Haley Aldrich. He stated that they are confident in what 
the study shows right now for their highest levels. He stated that if needed they can write 
something to limit the amount of nitrogen and fertilizer used on the grass in the condo 
documents.   
 
MOTION by Dr. Kaplan that the Board of Health approve the subdivision water quality study that 
is in front of them and that their models have adequately met the threshold of the regulation. 
Seconded by Mr. Dole. Carried 4-0.   
 
The Board agreed to have Mr. Smith send the approval letter and that the letter would also 
include comments that if there's any variance in modeling numbers, they would be willing to add 
actual site numbers, not modeling numbers. 
 
EWS Suitability Subcommittee Report and Guidance: 
 
Ms. Hurley stated that the EWS Suitability Subcommittee met twice since the last Board of 
Health meeting. She stated that at the first meeting they discussed the operational scope and 
the workflow with the primary goal of making sure they have transparent and consistent 
communication with the applicant and with counsel. She stated that they came up with a set of 
responsibilities that she would like the Board to review and approve. She stated that they want 
to build and maintain communication standards with Seaside Legal and the applicant to make 
sure that whenever they're communicating, with the City, ConCom, Planning Board, City 
Council, that they are included. She stated that they would like to propose a project status sheet 
so that they will be able to consistently communicate with the applicant and their counsel on 
exactly where they stand with each element of the 37 conditions and the deliverables that are
Page 4 
Minutes of the Board of Health 
July 9, 2026 
 
surrounding them. She stated that they agreed that the obligation of their meetings would be to 
meet in advance of a deliverable with the applicant to rely on form and format. She stated that 
the next thing they discussed was how do they provide guidance on site suitability, condition 
submissions, and actions that might be taken and so they aligned on the fact that this is 
unbiased; it's a fact based review of condition requirements. She stated that they are going to 
be leveraging the decision document only. She stated that they agreed that when the City is 
meeting regarding site suitability dynamics that there is a representative or a member of the 
subcommittee who would be sitting in and available to offer and represent that decision 
document. She stated that they agreed that the subcommittee meetings should be open 
meetings so that they have full transparency to the public and to the applicant. She stated that 
they agreed to report back to the Board, helping the Board understand status and providing 
detailed review of submissions, and confirming that they do or do not meet criteria. She stated 
that they will update the Board on a rolling basis.  
 
Ms. Hurley stated that at the second meeting they discussed internal departmental coordination 
and more specifics on communication protocols. She stated that they want to be sure that the 
site suitability decision in the case of the notice of intent is included in all third party reviews. 
She reviewed certain conditions with Board members that they believe hit different points, but 
are important for the Conservation Commission to consider to be sure that they are reviewing 
and considering as they look at the notes of intent. The Board discussed the possibility of 
adding a condition to suggest or make a suggestion to ConCom that they periodically monitor 
the stormwater that's running off into the wetlands. 
 
Ms. Hurley stated that the applicant has redone their wetlands mapping and there is actually 
significantly less property that's sitting in the buffer zone than originally anticipated.  
 
The Board agreed that the site suitability decision is explicitly included in all third party reviews, 
calling out not just the presence of the deliverable, but the rationale within the body of the 
decision that led to the need of that condition for consideration by that third party and that the 
Board of Health be welcomed at the Conservation Commission meeting to clarify the nuances of 
the site suitability criteria and the facts of the original decision and that they write a letter to the 
Conservation Commission to that effect and specifically call out, the concerns that are identified 
in Part 3, Section 11, 14 through 16, 20, 24, and 33, 32 and that they request the ability to make 
a presentation.  
 
Ms. Hurley stated that she will draft a letter on the Board’s behalf and send it, copying the 
members of the Board.  
 
Ms. Hurley stated that the subcommittee is going to implement a standardized review 
methodology, leveraging the status sheet; she went into detail on how the status sheet will work.   
 
Health Director’s Recap:
Page 5 
Minutes of the Board of Health 
July 9, 2026 
 
Ms. Hurley stated that the Health Department has a new Administrative Assistant, Alison Battle. 
She stated that Carla DellaPorta applied for and received the position in their prevention 
department as a program manager.  
 
Ms. Hurley stated that they had to change how they're counting things from reports and the 
reports they send to the State. She stated that the IT Department created a ticketing system for 
the Health Department to assist in creating reports.   
 
Ms. Hurley stated that a few months ago the Board voted to update the Subdivision Water 
Quality Assessment Regulation regulations and in the process of reviewing that document to 
send it to the State they found a random reference to the 2000 Wastewater regulations and 
another bit of stuff about subcommittees. She stated that they are pretty confident that that 
content is not needed, however, because it is documented in the regulation, they have to come 
back and propose another change to the regulation and hold another public hearing. 
 
Ms. Hurley stated that a letter went out in early June to the tobacco retailers reminding them 
that if they have products that are not FDA approved, they can't sell them. She stated that the 
FDA has a product database that retailers can use to confirm if the product has a Marketing 
Granted Order. She stated that the challenge is that some retailers have products sitting on the 
shelves without FDA clearance, and other retailers disposed of any inventory they shouldn't 
have. Some retailers are saying they have inventory that they want to sell down, and they have 
retailers that they haven't heard from, so they don't really know the status. She asked the Board 
for guidance on how they think they should approach enforcement.  
 
Mr. Dole noted that two weeks ago, a group of tobacco retailers filed a lawsuit in U.S. federal 
court against the Massachusetts Department of Public Health and 16 other municipalities—
though not Gloucester—to challenge their authority to enforce federal regulations. This legal 
action was prompted by enforcement letters similar to the one sent by the City of Gloucester. 
 
Mr. Rosa asked if they have any documentation from any of the retailers stating that they cannot 
return the product.  
 
Ms. Hurley responded that they have had retailer reaction to say, “Here's how much money I'll 
be out.”  
 
Mr. Markert stated that on a go-forward basis, retailers should only want to work with a 
distributor that can take back something that shouldn't be distributed in the first place.  
 
Mr. Dole stated that they are in limbo, at least in Massachusetts, with pending litigation that will 
not get resolved in the next few months; it might be a year, year and a half out, but there's a 
decision from the federal court specifically about this issue in Massachusetts. He stated that it's 
been litigated in other federal courts in other states.
Page 6 
Minutes of the Board of Health 
July 9, 2026 
 
Mr. Rosa stated that they could provide access to a physical list and a website for retailers, they 
could ask retailers for documentation from distributors stating that the product cannot be 
returned, or if they get to the place where they have to allow sell down of these illegals they 
could ask the retailers to put in place a plan that'll cost money to inform youth of the health 
issues regarding these products with a plan to be approved by the Health Department.  
 
Ms. Hurley stated that they could ask retailers to document exactly what products they have and 
how many so that they can keep track of that inventory, and then after an expiration time, 
there's zero tolerance. The Board agreed that the product that they buy from the distributor has 
to be on the approved list, or there has to be some documentation that shows otherwise.  
 
Sunny Patel appeared before the Board. He stated that he owns two smoke shops in 
Gloucester. He stated that they buy all their products within the State of Massachusetts and he 
pays 75% tax on those products. He stated that marijuana, soda, and other products are not on 
the FDA list but they are sold in Massachusetts.  
 
Ms. Hurley responded that Board of Health regulations and a retail permit both state that they 
have to apply to federal, state, and local regulations, and any product that they have on their 
shelves that is not approved by the federal government is therefore in defiance of federal law, 
which in turn is in defiance of their regulations. Ms. Hurley stated that it's illegal to sell products 
that are not FDA approved and it's further, even if they are FDA approved, illegal to sell those 
products in the state of Massachusetts if they have flavor. She stated that if they are selling a 
product that is not approved, there is a risk to their business, and they should be reporting any 
products that are in defiance of federal law to the FDA via their online portal. 
 
Ms. Hurley stated that the letter went out in June and the deadline was July 1 and the letter was 
delayed in going out so that left a two week time frame for retailers to comply. Mr. Dole 
described the legal issue surrounding this topic that is occurring in Beverly.  
 
Neil Warner of 67 Dollivers Neck Drive, appeared before the Board. He stated that he used to 
own a biochemistry company and had many products go through him. He stated that they do 
not approve products, they approve products for marketing, so that's different. Mr. Dole 
responded that the issue is the FDA is lagging far, far behind the issue of the marketing and 
branding orders for these new styles of tobacco products, vapes, and pouches.  
 
Mr. Dole stated that they can ask retailers to provide documentation of the products they have 
on the shelf. Chairperson Rosa stated that they have to put together some process that has to 
be vetted that they could add to their annual permitting process.  
 
The Board agreed that having some information about why they bought illegal products would 
be useful to know.
Page 7 
Minutes of the Board of Health 
July 9, 2026 
 
Ms. Hurley stated that they can work with retailers who have issues with these products to figure 
out why they have the product and come back with a recommendation on how they can move 
forward.  
 
Ms. Hurley stated that they have goals as part of their budget and the administration is now 
working with all the department heads on figuring out how they attend those goals. She stated 
that none of our goals are new and they have been working on them for a while. 
 
Ms. Hurley stated that Ms. Larabee has a briefing which is included in the packet, which is an 
assessment of how they did on a state performance against public health excellence norms. 
She stated that she will give the briefing at the next Board meeting. 
 
Ms. White gave an update on the Brian Pollard case with the 10 rental properties. She stated 
that five properties were randomly inspected at the Board’s request and they had good 
outcomes. She stated that she was impressed with his process and the way he was running his 
businesses. The Board agreed that these five inspections were a good representation and no 
further inspections are required. 
 
 
Prevention Team Reporting: 
 
Ms. Goldstein-Walsh stated that they are in the process of reapplying for a federal grant due 
next week. She stated that if they receive it, it would be a five-year grant which focuses on 
substance use prevention across seven communities on the North Shore. She stated that it's 
$250,000 a year for five years.  
 
Ms. Goldstein-Walsh stated that Carla Dellaporta will be joining their team later this month. 
 
Dr. Kaplan asked about the Risk Behavior Survey. Ms. Goldstein-Walsh responded that they 
are waiting for the final data report. She stated that she needs to get permission before she can 
share the data in a public forum.  
 
Concerns of the Board: 
 
Next Regular Monthly Meeting Board of Health- The next regular Board of Health meeting is 
scheduled for Thursday, August 6, 2026 at 5:30 pm.  
 
MOTION by Dr. Kaplan to adjourn. 
Seconded by Mr. Dole CARRIED. 
MEETING ADJOURNED – 7:59 p.m. 
 
  
Respectfully submitted, 
________________________________
Page 8 
Minutes of the Board of Health 
July 9, 2026 
 
  
Bobbi Orlando 
  
Accepted by: 
  
_________________________________
